newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Gle des Eaux to fund Hungary concessions.
newsitem.headline: Gle des Eaux to fund Hungary concessions.

text.p: The French utility group Compagnie Generale des Eaux and other investors are to boost development funds for two local telephone concession operators in Hungary by some $260 million, officials said on Monday.

"CGSAT, Giltek, GE Capital and other major investors have reached agreement on Friday for the equity financing of the Hungarian local telephone operators Digitel 2002 and Deltav," Digitel said in a statement.
Digitel and Deltav started their operations in 1995 with 95,000 telephone lines, which they plan to increase to 175,000 this year and to 300,000 by the turn of the century.
The statement added that CGSAT, a subsidiary of Compagnie Generale, would remain the largest shareholder and provide the management of the concession companies.
Giltek, an Israeli company active in the telecommunications sector, was a founding shareholder of Digitel, the statement said.
GE is one of the largest foreign investors in Hungary, with investments in the bulb maker Tungsram and Budapest Bank.
Digitel and Deltav previously signed loans totalling $137 million with the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development.
"This equity agreement will complete the total financing of the project estimated at $400 million," the statement added.
